primitives.name: Event Detection via Entropy Loss
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Event detection: scan text corpora for words and up-to-three-word phrases with high expected entropy loss (information gain) around market-move dates; three case studies show meaningful event terms surfacing.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'IG': 'expected information gain (dimensionless)', 'w': 'term (word or phrase)', 'P(w)': 'probability of term w (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Text corpora contain causal events; information arrives exogenously; market moves are driven by event terms.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When P(w) approaches zero or information gain becomes negligible.

layer2.mapping: Maps textual entropy loss to market event labels via probabilistic information gain ranking.
layer2.telemetry: Top-ranked terms correlate with known market-moving events.

primitives.name: Martingale Forecast Accuracy
primitives.verbatim_quote: Equations & assumptions - Martingale (forecast accuracy): E[p_t | p_{t-1} = a] = a.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p_t': 'market price at time t (dimensionless)', 'p_{t-1}': 'market price at time t-1 (dimensionless)', 'a': 'price level (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Prices are unbiased forecasts; no risk premia or favorite-longshot bias.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When conditional expectation fails due to endogeneity or feedback loops.

layer2.mapping: Price evolution as a stochastic process with no predictable drift, mirroring random walk dynamics.
layer2.telemetry: Log-score linearity over time in validation markets.

primitives.name: Winner-Conditioned Price Update
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Winner-conditioned update: E[p_t | E, p_{t-1} = a] = a + Var(p_t | p_{t-1} = a)/a.
primitives.latex: E[p_t | E, p_{t-1} = a] = a + \frac{\text{Var}(p_t | p_{t-1} = a)}{a}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p_t': 'market price at time t (dimensionless)', 'E': 'event occurrence (boolean)', 'a': 'previous price level (dimensionless)', 'Var(p_t | p_{t-1} = a)': 'variance of price change given previous price (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Events induce variance-dependent price shifts; price changes are conditionally normal.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When variance becomes undefined or price exceeds bounds.

layer2.mapping: Conditional price shift modeled as variance-adjusted deviation from prior price.
layer2.telemetry: Empirical winner/loser movement ratio matches e^ε.

primitives.name: Log-Likelihood Price Space
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Log-likelihood space: work with logit(p) = ln(p/(1-p)); price changes in this space approximately symmetric, power-law distributed.
primitives.assumptions: Price changes are symmetric in logit space; increments follow power law.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At p = 0 or p = 1 where logit diverges.

layer2.mapping: Transforms asymmetric price dynamics into symmetric, analyzable space for modeling.
layer2.telemetry: Power-law distribution of log-likelihood price increments.

reasoning_traces.think: Chapter 2 introduces a framework for modeling information incorporation in financial markets using entropy-based event detection, martingale price dynamics, and log-likelihood transformations. The core idea is that market prices reflect the cumulative effect of information arrivals, which can be detected through text analysis. The model assumes unbiased forecasts and exogenous information flow, enabling the use of martingale principles to describe price evolution. Entropy loss quantifies how much new information a term contributes to explaining price movements. The log-likelihood transformation ensures symmetric treatment of price changes, facilitating power-law modeling of increments. Validation relies on qualitative agreement between theoretical predictions and empirical data from 22 IEM markets, including log-score linearity, late acceleration, and winner/loser ratios. This approach bridges natural language processing and financial modeling through a unified probabilistic lens.
